# @ashstack/lint rules

Start here, then open only the page relevant to the task. For a diagnostic such as `@ashstack/unistyles/no-margin`, open the `@ashstack/unistyles` page and follow its rule index. Each rule states its default status, options, and examples where available.

`core()`, `react()` and `react-native()` each contain the one before, so a section's built-in table lists only the settings that entry changes. Built-in rules link to their upstream page.

Turn any rule off by id in your own `rules` block: `"@ashstack/unistyles/no-margin": "off"`.

Each entry lists the oxlint plugins it turns on, below. You never need to add them: your own `plugins` array is added to the entry's set, not swapped for it. A bare oxlint install runs `eslint`, `typescript`, `unicorn`, `oxc`; `import`, `promise`, `react`, `jsx-a11y`, `react-perf` come from here.

Counting what each entry sets with every module on: **116** rules for plain TypeScript, **211** with React, **268** on React Native, 82 of them written for this package. oxlint's own `correctness` category runs alongside these.

## Entry settings

| Read when | Page |
| --- | --- |
| Any TypeScript project — backend, CLI, library. Built-in settings and plugins. | [`core()`](rules/entries/core.md) |
| React on the web. Adds the you-might-not-need-an-effect rules as `@ashstack/effects/`, alongside oxlint's own react plugin. Built-in settings and plugins. | [`react()`](rules/entries/react.md) |
| Expo and React Native. Built-in settings and plugins. | [`react-native()`](rules/entries/react-native.md) |
